name: universal-prompt-gate-mcp

tools.name: rewrite_prompt
tools.description:
Re-emit the given prompt with richer context, structure, and quality criteria. This tool only produces a candidate rewrite; it does NOT approve the result. Use review_and_select_prompt for the gated, user-confirmed flow.

CALLING GUIDE (for the LLM):
- ALWAYS pass a short `context` (1-3 sentences) summarizing the conversation/session so far so the enrichment is grounded. Do not omit it.
- Choose `rewrite_level` to fit the task: `light` for quick one-shot answers, `balanced` (default) for most coding/research work, `detailed` when the user explicitly wants a fully-specified spec.
- ALWAYS pass `language` set to the language of the user's original prompt (e.g. "vietnamese"), so the rewrite stays in that language. If the user explicitly asks for a different output language, pass that language instead. Do NOT switch the language on your own judgment — that is a drift.

prompt.description: The original prompt to rewrite. This is the user's latest message only.

language.description: Output language of the rewritten prompt, e.g. "vietnamese", "english", "japanese". ALWAYS pass the language the user wrote their prompt in, so the rewrite preserves it. If the user explicitly asks for a different output language (e.g. "answer in English"), pass THAT language instead. Never switch the language on your own judgment — passing "english" to "improve clarity" is a drift. Omit only when the language cannot be determined; the server then auto-detects it.

context.description: 1-3 sentences summarizing the conversation/session so far (what the user has asked, what files/topics are in play, what was decided). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: pass this on every call so the rewrite is grounded in prior context. Omit only for brand-new sessions with no history.

rewrite_level.description: How much enrichment to apply. "light" = minimal (keep close to original); "balanced" (default) = add missing structure/context/criteria; "detailed" = full spec with acceptance criteria. Pick based on task complexity.

tools.name: review_and_select_prompt
tools.description:
Generates a rewritten version of the prompt, then asks the user to choose: use original, use rewritten, request changes (update), or cancel. Returns only the approved prompt. Cancellation is a distinct outcome and never exposes an approved prompt.

Before the rewrite, the USER chooses the enrichment level (`rewrite_level`: light / balanced / detailed) via an interactive picker — the agent must not choose it. If the client does not support MCP elicitation, the tool returns a distinct "pending_level_selection" result with the level menu in plain text; ask the user, then re-call with the SAME inputs PLUS `rewrite_level` set to their choice. Never pick for the user.

After the rewrite, if the client does not support MCP elicitation, the tool returns a distinct "pending_user_selection" result: it shows both versions in plain text with the numbered choices and asks the agent to re-call this tool with `selection` set to the user's choice ("original" / "rewritten" / "update" / "cancel"). Choosing "update" is not final: pass the user's requested changes in `feedback`, the tool rewrites again and returns a NEW "pending_user_selection" to review. Repeat until the user picks original, rewritten, or cancel. Never auto-select.

CALLING GUIDE (for the LLM):
- FIRST call: pass prompt + context (+ language); do NOT pass `rewrite_level` and do NOT pass `selection` — the user chooses the level. ALWAYS pass a short `context` (1-3 sentences) summarizing the conversation so far.
- If a call returns status "pending_level_selection": ask the user which level to use, then call again with the SAME inputs PLUS `rewrite_level` set to "light", "balanced", or "detailed" matching their choice.
- If a call returns status "pending_user_selection": show the two versions to the user, ask which to use, then call again with the SAME inputs PLUS `selection` set to "original", "rewritten", or "cancel" matching the user's choice. If the user wants changes instead ("update"), call again with `selection: "update"` PLUS `feedback` containing their requested changes (and `rewritten_prompt` of the version they reviewed); the tool replies with a new "pending_user_selection". Loop until the user picks original, rewritten, or cancel — never decide for them.
- ALWAYS pass `language` set to the language of the user's original prompt (e.g. "vietnamese"), so the rewrite stays in that language. If the user explicitly asks for a different output language, pass that language instead. Do NOT switch the language on your own judgment — that is a drift.

prompt.description: The original prompt to review. This is the user's latest message only.

language.description: Output language of the rewritten prompt, e.g. "vietnamese", "english", "japanese". ALWAYS pass the language the user wrote their prompt in, so the rewrite preserves it. If the user explicitly asks for a different output language (e.g. "answer in English"), pass THAT language instead. Never switch the language on your own judgment — passing "english" to "improve clarity" is a drift. Omit only when the language cannot be determined; the server then auto-detects it.

context.description: 1-3 sentences summarizing the conversation/session so far (what the user has asked, what files/topics are in play, what was decided). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED: pass this on every call so the rewrite is grounded in prior context. Omit only for brand-new sessions with no history.

rewrite_level.description: The enrichment level used for the rewrite. The USER chooses it via an interactive picker (or via the "pending_level_selection" text menu when the client has no elicitation), so do NOT pass it on the first call. Only pass it to relay the user's explicit choice on the call AFTER a "pending_level_selection" result: "light" (minimal), "balanced" (adds structure/context/criteria), or "detailed" (full spec with acceptance criteria).

selection.description: ONLY for a re-call after a pending_user_selection flow: the user's explicit choice after the server could not show an interactive picker. On the first call (rewrite) this must be omitted. Values: "original", "rewritten", "cancel", or "update" (the user wants changes: pass their request in `feedback`; the tool rewrites again and returns a NEW "pending_user_selection"). Never auto-select; pass it only after the user has chosen.

rewritten_prompt.description: The exact rewritten text the user saw. Pass it with `selection`="rewritten" (this is what gets approved — the user approves exactly what they read) and with `selection`="update" (the previous rewrite to revise). Omit on the first call.

feedback.description: ONLY with selection="update": the changes the user asked for, in their own words (e.g. "make it shorter", "add acceptance criteria for X", "keep the tone casual"). The tool applies them in the next rewrite. Required when selection="update". Never invent feedback for the user.

tools.name: get_client_capabilities
tools.description: Reports which interaction features are available for the current MCP client/session: elicitation support, structured elicitation, transport, integration mode, and whether a mandatory prompt gate is enforceable. Capabilities are derived from verified protocol negotiation, not from the agent name.
